results.summary_before: This project implements a 3-bit arithmetic logic unit (ALU) that performs arithmetic and logical operations on two 3-bit binary numbers, selected by two select lines. It is built in Wokwi and uses eight inputs: six for operands a and b, and two for the operation select. The outputs drive a seven-segment display to show the result, with the display exhibiting a random sequence on startup until the circuit settles after two clock cycles. External hardware required is a seven-segment display, and the design serves as an educational example of a basic ALU.

results.summary_before: This design continuously transmits a looping serial bit stream and detects a hardcoded 9-bit birthday pattern within it, counting hits per second and displaying the count on two 7-segment digits. Transmission is enabled by an active-low input, and a valid pulse indicates when the hit count is updated each second. The design requires external 7-segment displays for the tens and units digits, and no other custom hardware. The documentation is detailed and includes step-by-step test instructions, though the design is essentially a fixed-pattern detector with limited configurability.

results.summary_before: MAW Bird Shooter is a single-player arcade game implemented in SystemVerilog that drives a 640x480 60 Hz VGA display directly from the chip. The player moves a crosshair with four directional buttons and fires up to ten shots at an animated bird, with hit/miss overlays, a shot counter, and win/lose screens. It requires a VGA monitor or TinyVGA PMOD, five momentary push-buttons, and five 10 kOhm pull-down resistors on the button inputs. The design is notable for fitting a complete game with sprite rendering, LFSR-driven enemy movement, and button debouncing into a 2x2 tile ASIC.
